text:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT PAGER — P0: ELB 5xx spike in euc2 (eu-central-2) AZf affecting redwood-prod-frontend. Alert: >=5% 5xx over 5m. See: https://pagerduty.example/incident/INC-4067890123 :rotating_light:

maria (oncall): acked. taking initial triage. I see 502/504s on the ELB fronting the frontend fleet, spike started ~09:18 UTC.

shane: oncall-east here — joining. any customer-reported pages?

support-bot: 4 high-severity customer reports opened in last 10m mentioning 'site unavailable' and elevated error rates in EU. Top customers: AcmeCorp, BrightShop.

maria (oncall): running quick checks. curl from eu node:
```
curl -sv https://frontend.eu.redwood.example/health || true
* Connected to frontend.eu.redwood.example (10.0.23.111) port 443 (#0)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: frontend.eu.redwood.example
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json
{ "status": "bad_gateway" }
```

leo: logs from target group show backend instances healthy but ELB returning 502s during TLS handshake timeouts. sample from lb logs:
```
type=requestelb time=2026-02-28T09:19:05.123Z elb=app/redwood-prod-elb-1 ... target_status=504 target: timed out connecting to backend
```

maria (oncall): interesting — backend app instances report normal CPU and successful local health checks. Could be a networking plane between ELB and ENI or cross-AZ routing.

opsbot: AWS status page update found: eu-central-2 networking degradation in AZf (partial) — https://status.aws.amazon.com/incidents/abcdefg. last updated 09:21 UTC.

aws-status-bot: Status: "Investigating - Partial networking disruption in eu-central-2 AZf affecting ENI reachability and EC2 API responses."

shane: that matches. Are we seeing >1 AZ impacted or only AZf?

maria (oncall): traffic graph shows spike only from AZf edge nodes. Other AZs stable. Route53 health checks for regional endpoints show increased latency from EU vantage points that hit AZf-backed ELBs.

danielle: suggest we fail traffic away from AZf by adjusting Route53 weight and ELB AZ routing if possible. Also prepare dedicated note for customers.

leo: We can shift weight via Route53 by updating weighted routing policy for frontend.europeal. I'll prepare a quick change: set AZf-backed record weight to 0, increase other AZ weights. Applying in 30s will incur DNS TTL propagation. Current TTL is 60s.

maria (oncall): do it. Also open a mitigation ticket for Dedicated capacity customers who bind to specific AZs.

shane: before changing, confirm we have capacity in other AZs for extra load. autoscaler shows spare capacity across AZa/AZb. autoscaling group for frontend has room +20%.

leo: applying Route53 change now (change-id: Z1234567890).

opsbot: Route53 change submitted: change-id Z1234567890. Expected propagation ~30-90s given current TTL.

maria (oncall): creating incident in status page and drafting customer comms: "We're investigating increased error rates from eu-central-2 AZf. Traffic is being routed to healthy AZs; we expect recovery within minutes."

support-bot: Sent initial templated note to impacted customers (AcmeCorp, BrightShop). Included link to status page and workaround guidance.

leo: after weight shift, per-edge metrics show 5xx rate dropping from 7% -> 1.2% over 2 minutes for EU edge nodes hitting alternative AZs.

shane: good. Are we still seeing ENI disconnects or just latency?

leo: ENI health metrics in AZf showing intermittent transmit drops, ENI-to-host keepalive failures — consistent with partial ISP/peering degradation inside AZf.

maria (oncall): so root likely AWS network/ISP path affecting AZf interconnects with regional edge. We'll keep routing away from AZf until AWS confirms fix.

danielle: I'll take ownership for the next shift and handle customer comms + post-incident summary. maria, want to handoff incident to me?

maria (oncall): handing off to danielle for sustained mitigation and communications. I'm staying on-call if you need escalation.

danielle: taking. updating incident channel and pager. setting incident state: mitigating. adding runbook tag: runbook/elbs/route53-weight-shift.

opsbot: conference bridge created: +1-555-0123 ext 406789 for incident INC-4067890123.

support-bot: Notifying account execs for impacted customers and offering SRE assist if they require deeper root-cause during outage.

danielle: monitoring for 15m. if 5xx < 1% and customer reports cleared, we'll declare mitigation.

aws-status-bot: AWS update 09:34 UTC — "Fix in progress; traffic restoration underway for impacted peering links in eu-central-2 AZf."

leo: observed slow reduction of ENI errors in AZf starting 09:36. 5xx now 0.4%.

support-bot: all open customer tickets related to this incident have been acknowledged and provided mitigation guidance.

danielle: preparing incident timeline + immediate action items: 1) route53 weight shift at 09:20 UTC, 2) capacity verified in other AZs, 3) engaged AWS for root cause, 4) customer comms sent. Will continue to collect logs and metric snapshots for postmortem.

maria (oncall): marking as 'monitoring'. good work. If AWS confirms fully recovered, we'll start recovery and an RCA runbook.

aws-status-bot: 09:44 UTC — "Resolved: Networking peering fully restored in eu-central-2 AZf. Services returning to normal."

danielle: observed full stabilization across EU endpoints by 09:46. no further customer errors reported. closing mitigation at 09:46 UTC. I'll own postmortem and follow up with AWS support for timeline of the ISP/peering issue.

maria (oncall): thanks team. I'll hand incident to SRE postmortem board. cc @oncall-sre for RCA. :white_check_mark:

shane: nice runbook execution. recommend adding a quick play for 'partial AZ ISP peering' to the ELB runbook to make weight-shift steps more explicit.

danielle: noted — will add doc and include change diff for automated Route53 weight toggles in the runbook.

opsbot: Incident INC-4067890123 status: Resolved. Duration: 28 minutes. Participants: maria (oncall), shane, leo, danielle.

maria (oncall): closing channel thread. will post postmortem link when ready.

shane: thanks all. :heart:
